Every warning/error a user can hit in normal operation must state: what degraded,
what stops working, and the ONE command that fixes it.

   recall/query output (brief "warnings" array, setup_status.go states, host_cli.go,
   facts_integrity.go, filelock errors in internal/config and internal/cli). Known
   states: graph/semantic provider absent; host entire CLI not on PATH; manifest
   behind store; hardlinked history index (filelock refusal); stale/missing index;
   branch has no memories (brief suggests --branch retry); NO_EGRESS/LOCAL_ONLY
   suppression; repo identity conflict. Expect a few more — list what you find.

   removes history context from every brief). Determine the actual repair (does

   message name it, and if no repair exists, propose one in the PR before building it.

   one-line hint in `status` and brief warnings when the semantic provider is absent:

   the entire CLI plugin flow (verify the real command; do not invent it). Also
   verify what happens when an INCOMPATIBLE graph version is present — the pinning
   guidance is >=1.0 <2.0 provider schema — and that the error names the required
   version.
5. Human output goes through internal/tui; JSON warning strings are a compat
   surface — changing their wording is fine, changing JSON keys/structure is not.

# Degraded-state messages: name what broke, what stops working, and the one fix command

Stable-release gate (v0.2.0): every warning a user can hit in normal operation
must match the shape of `facts_integrity.go`'s manifest warning — what
degraded, what stops working, the one command that fixes it. This PR audits
the degraded states, fixes the messages where a remedy exists, and builds the
one repair that was missing.

## The priority case was real and unfixable

`history index must not be hardlinked: <path>` fires in the wild: an external
tool hardlink-copied the live brain's `history/` tree (found on a dev machine:
a bench harness staged a clone under `/tmp/cor2214-bench/`, which raises nlink
on the LIVE files). The alias guard then refuses every read and history
context silently drops out of each brief. Worse, **no command could clear
it**:

- `memory repair` failed on the same guard (`memory_state_unsafe` on the
  hardlinked receipt) before reaching its rebuild;
- `refresh` and the memory worker hit the identical refusal at the publish
  commit (`active history projection receipts are unsafe and read-only`);
- generation pruning skipped the directory forever.

Fix: an UNSAFE receipt (hardlinked/symlinked/swapped) no longer vetoes repair
or publish — the rebuild never reads it and derives a fresh generation from
the canonical sessions. Only `unsupported` (vNext schema) receipts stay fatal:
data this binary cannot decode must not be rebuilt over. Pruning now removes a
generation whose receipt is hardlink-unreadable (removal only unlinks our
dirent; the external link keeps its bytes). The refusal classifies via a new
`errFileHardlinked` sentinel; rendered text is unchanged.

## Message table

| state | trigger | message before | message after | fix command |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hardlinked history index/receipt (brief, recall, query) | external hardlink copy of `history/` | `history context unavailable: history index must not be hardlinked: <path>` | same + `— history context is dropped from briefs and recall until the projection is rebuilt; run `entire brain memory repair`` | `memory repair` (now actually works) |
| unsafe projection receipt (`memory status` action) | same | `inspect the manifest receipt path; remove the unsafe pointer before repair` | `run `entire brain memory repair` — the unsafe receipt is never read; a fresh generation is rebuilt from canonical sessions` | `memory repair` |
| semantic index missing, graph provider absent (brief) | provider never installed | `semantic index missing; run `entire brain refresh`` (refresh cannot build it) | `semantic index missing: the graph provider is not installed, so code context and semantic queries are skipped — install it with `entire plugin install graph`, then run `entire brain refresh index`` | `entire plugin install graph` |
| same (status next step) | same | `run `entire brain refresh --agent none`` | `the graph provider is not installed, so code context and semantic queries are skipped; install it with `entire plugin install graph`, then run `entire brain refresh index`` | `entire plugin install graph` |
| provider schema major out of pin (>=1.0 <2.0) | graph/brain version skew | `unsupported semantic schema major version "2": this build reads semantic schema >=1.0 <2.0` | same + `— the provider is ahead of this build; upgrade entire-brain` (or, for an old provider, `… behind this build; upgrade it with `entire plugin install graph``) | direction-dependent |
| provider schema version malformed | broken provider output | `… (this build reads semantic schema >=1.0 <2.0)` | same + `; reinstall the provider with `entire plugin install graph`` | `entire plugin install graph` |
| branch memory store unreadable (brief) | per-branch facts file damaged | `memory store for <branch> unavailable: <err>` | same + `; its memories cannot be recalled — run `entire brain refresh` and re-distill` | `refresh` |
| no-egress export skips (3 warnings) | `ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS` set | `no_egress: branch checkpoint fallback skipped` | same + `— checkpoints not already local are left out while ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS is set` (each names the var actually set) | unset the named var |
| no-egress export refusals (2 errors) | same, catalog incomplete | `…; refusing a false-empty export` | same + `— unset ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS to allow it` | unset the named var |

`no_egress:`, `memory_state_unsafe:` and the other code prefixes are machine
contracts and are unchanged; only prose after the prefix moved. No JSON key or
structure changed (`statusHealth` is render-only; brief warnings are strings).

The graph provider probe (`semanticProviderOnHost`) runs only in the
already-degraded state (semantic index missing) and only when the host CLI is
present, so `status`/brief pay nothing on the healthy path.

## Flagged: degraded states with NO remediation path (not text-fixable)

1. **The generic `"X unavailable: " + err` wrap class** — ~17 brief/live
   warning sites (`agent_surface.go`). The honest fix is enriching the error
   at its source, as done here for history artifacts; a wrap-site command
   would guess.
2. **File-lock timeouts** (`filelock.go`, 12 lock codes) — name the holder pid
   but no action (wait/retry/kill is situational).
3. **`memory_unsupported_version` / newer-schema refusals** — the remedy
   (upgrade the brain binary) has no stable in-product command to name;
   doctor's upgrade remedy covers it interactively.
4. **`fact review queue unreadable; verify fact consistency…`** — names no
   command, and none exists.
5. **5 of 6 freshness axes** leave their `Remedy` field empty
   (`agent_surface.go:4686-4716`).
6. **7 of 9 `semanticDoctorFailureError` branches** (`semantic.go:701-721`)
   state the cause without a command.
7. **Dead code**: `semanticRefreshNeeded`'s identity warning is hardcoded `""`
   on every path (`refresh.go:728-752`), so its `warning: %s` print is
   unreachable.
8. **Root cause upstream**: bench/CI tooling that clones brain state should
   use APFS clonefile (`cp -c`) or a real copy, never hardlinks — a hardlink
   mutates the nlink of the LIVE store it copies.

## Validation

- New regression test `TestMemoryRepairRecoversHardlinkedHistoryProjection`:
  hardlinks a published generation externally, asserts the read error names
  `memory repair`, repair rebuilds, the hardlinked generation is pruned, and
  the external clone keeps its files.
- New `TestStatusNextStepNamesGraphInstallWhenProviderAbsent`.
- Validated against the real degraded brain on the affected machine: with this
  build, `memory repair --dry-run` reports `would_rebuild: true` (previously
  failed with `memory_state_unsafe`), and the brief warning carries the
  remedy.
- Full `go test ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt -s` clean; Windows cross-build clean.

input.title: Adopt enrich-at-source convention for brief's generic "X unavailable: <err>" warnings
input.description:
The brief and live-state warning arrays contain ~17 sites in `internal/cli/agent_surface.go` that wrap an arbitrary error as `"<thing> unavailable: " + err.Error()` (blind spots, semantic context, runtime trace, test suggestions, global memories, memories, freshness, HEAD/branch/diff probes, …). None states what stops working or what command fixes it. A wrap-site remedy would guess: the wrap cannot know why the underlying read failed.

PR https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/458 established the honest pattern for history artifacts: classify the failure at its source with a sentinel (`errFileHardlinked`) and attach the remedy there, so every surface that wraps it inherits the full sentence.

Work:
- Adopt this as the convention: degraded-state errors carry their own remedy at the point where the cause is known.
- Seed it with the highest-traffic wraps where the remedy is knowable: `memories unavailable` / `global memories unavailable` (store integrity → refresh + re-distill) and `semantic context unavailable` (provider/doctor errors already carry remedies after #458's follow-up).
- Leave wraps whose causes are genuinely heterogeneous as-is.

Inventory of all sites and their current texts: PR #458 description, "Flagged" section.

input.title: Fact review queue (proposals.json) has no recovery path when unreadable
input.description:
When `proposals.json` cannot be read, every surface shows `fact review queue unreadable; verify fact consistency before relying on these facts` (`retrieval_guard.go`, `facts_read_cmd.go`, brief warnings; unified-path caveat code `proposal_state_unavailable`). The message names no command because none exists — and unlike the history projection, this is not text-fixable: proposals are user data (pending reviews), not a derived projection, so no rebuild can recover them.

Design decision needed: should there be an explicit escape hatch, e.g. quarantine the unreadable file and start an empty queue behind an explicit acknowledge-loss flag (`memories review --reset-queue` or similar)? Until that exists, the degraded state is permanent and the message can only state the effect.

Context: flagged in the v0.2.0 degraded-state message audit, PR https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/458 ("Flagged" section, item 4).

input.title: Bench tooling must not hardlink-clone live brain state (use clonefile or a real copy)
input.description:
Found in the wild on a dev machine: a bench run (staged under `/tmp/cor2214-bench/data6/`, likely the COR-2214 harness) copied the live brain's `history/` tree with hardlinks. A hardlink raises nlink on the LIVE file it copies, which trips entire-brain's nlink>1 alias guard — every history read is then refused and history context silently drops out of each brief, recall, and query on the real brain.

PR https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/458 makes that state repairable (`entire brain memory repair`) and makes the refusal name the fix, but the harness keeps re-creating the condition on every run.

Fix in the bench tooling: replace the hardlink clone with APFS clonefile (`cp -c` on macOS) or a plain copy. Clonefile gives the same cheap copy-on-write semantics without touching the source files' link counts.

Relation to COR-2214: this issue is about the harness's clone step, not the benchmark itself.
